relatedSnapshot.title: Match older AI SDR escalations to their run when the run didn't record its campaign
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The older-notification backfill can't link AI SDR escalations sent before 31 August 2026, because the AI SDR runs from that period never recorded their campaign in the column the match reads. The campaign is saved elsewhere on the same run. Reading it from there would let about 32,000 older escalations be linked and stop holding about 1,050 people on Name 6.

## Problem

The report-only run of the backfill from ENG-14408 finished on 2 October 2026. Its biggest blocker is 32,450 older AI SDR escalations with no matching run, keeping 1,055 people on Name 6.

An escalation is linked only when exactly one escalated run fits its campaign, prospect and send time. Production shows that AI SDR runs started before 31 August 2026 13:35 UTC have an empty campaign column. It was empty for every run from May until then. So no escalation from before then can match, even though its run exists.

## Proposed fix

When a run's campaign column is empty, the backfill uses the campaign recorded in that run's saved starting state. Everything else in the match stays the same. Then run the report-only pass again and review it before the real run.

## What's included

* The escalation match in the backfill job, and a fresh report-only run in production with its results posted here.
* Excludes: writing to `execution_runs` (no data repair), changing other match rules, campaigns that were deleted (still blocked as missing), the real (writing) run, and ENG-13839 step D.
* Related: ENG-11733 owns recording the campaign on runs going forward.

## How it should work

* A run with an empty campaign column counts for the campaign in its saved starting state.
* A run with the column filled uses the column, as today. Production shows both agree for every newer escalated run (11,996 of 11,996).
* The rest of the rule is unchanged: same workspace, same prospect, started in the 15 minutes before the notification, still running when it was sent, exactly one such run. Zero or more than one fitting run still leaves the item blocked with its reason.
* Report-only by default, one person at a time, nothing sent, nothing written to Name 6.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: an internal job run by engineering, with no new access.

## What the user sees

Nothing directly. After the real run, older escalations move to the new list with their original time and state, and far fewer people stay on Name 6.

## Done when

* An escalation whose run has an empty campaign column but a matching campaign in its starting state is linked, and a test covers it.
* A run whose starting-state campaign belongs to another workspace is not used.
* The new report-only run shows `legacy_escalation_run_missing` down from 32,450 to a small remainder, and its results are posted here.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Most older AI SDR escalations can be linked, so the real run moves most of the people this blocker holds on Name 6.

## Implementation context

* Evidence, all read-only, 2 October 2026:
  * Escalated runs started 31 May to 31 August 13:35 UTC: 37,224. All have a campaign in `initial_state.campaignId`; 34,894 of them point to a campaign that still exists in the run's workspace.
  * Sample of 508 older escalations from owners of the 12 workspaces with the most older escalations: 0 match today, 505 match exactly one run with the fallback, 0 match more than one.
  * Newer escalations in the same sample: 152 of 152 match either way.
* Code: `listEscalatedRunCandidates` in `packages/db/src/repositories/legacy-receipt-candidate-repository.ts` reads `execution_runs.campaign_id`; `selectEscalationRun` in `apps/web/lib/notifications/personal/legacy-receipt-match.ts` compares it.
* AI context.md holds the production evidence, the match simulation, the suggested change and the test plan as of 2 October 2026.

relatedSnapshot.title: Refund/credit request: 15 of 36 paid inboxes in Error and not sending, one month of compensation requested
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Customer reports (2026-09-21/22) that several mailboxes have shown an error and have not been sending for over a month; the count has grown from 6 to 15. He says he has opened several support tickets for the same issue without resolution, that a teammate's fix (reactivating the inboxes) did not work, and that the problem is consuming his time. He asks to have the 15 failing inboxes deleted and replaced with working ones, and to be refunded / credited for one month of all 15 being down. He sent screenshots of the Cold Email Agent email-accounts page.

## Ask

Taxonomy bucket: refund. Requested financial remedy: be compensated for one month of 15 paid inboxes that were in Error and not sending. Alternative remedy the customer may prefer: a credit on the account rather than money back. Open human decision.

## Finding

15 of the workspace's 36 paid sending inboxes are in provider error and silent; the 21 healthy inboxes still send normally. The 15 carry the known ColdMailReseller / Zapmail reconnect defect: the reconnect path cannot resolve a mailbox the provider accepts ("Mailbox not found"), so the inbox never returns to Active. Four of them had already failed by mid-August 2026 and the rest failed from 19 September 2026. The workspace keeps paying the monthly fee for all 36.

## Exposure

Verified from billing records: 36 inbox spend items are active on the account at 8 USD per inbox per month (two active inbox subscriptions, 18 on each, with 36 of 36 inbox entitlements consumed). One month of 15 inboxes is about 120 USD of the account's monthly spend. The monthly plan fee and the healthy inboxes are unaffected. No refund or credit note has previously been issued on this account for these charges.

## Proposed action (proposal, never a promise)

A person on the support/billing side should decide and, if approved, issue a one-month compensation for the 15 affected inboxes (about 120 USD), in the form the customer wants: money back on the card, or an account credit consumed by the next invoice. Separately, a person should arrange the repair or replacement of the 15 inboxes, because replacing them is a paid provisioning action. Do not move money from this investigation.

## Systems of record

* Production workspace state: 33 inbox rows, 21 active/connected and 12 in Error; three further provider accounts exist with no local row. All 36 provider accounts are present in the workspace sub-workspace; 15 report a failed status with autofix_failed.
* Provider state: the 15 accounts are flagged errored at the provider itself, so the durable failure is not a missing provider account.
* Provisioning and entitlements: both inbox subscriptions are active, 36 of 36 inbox entitlements consumed; plan is Legacy Pro plus inbox and domain add-ons. No cancellation or deletion is in flight.
* Money movement: monthly invoices for 36 inboxes have been paid continuously; no refunds or credit notes exist on the account.
* First divergent hop: none. All three systems agree, so the remaining question is human discretion on the remedy.

## Approval trail

none found. No prior approval or promise to compensate, and no prior refund or credit for this outage, appears in the conversation or in the account's billing records.

## Justification checklist

1. The charge matches real invoices and active subscriptions - verified.
2. The disputed amount is quantified from primary billing data - verified (about 120 USD for one month of 15 inboxes at 8 USD each).
3. Plan and add-on state matches the account and production - verified.
4. Product-credit balance and prior-credit history were read from production - verified; no compensation credit is present.
5. A prior approval or promise is quoted, or explicitly absent - verified absent.
6. The ask is one taxonomy bucket - refund, with an account credit named as the customer's possible preference; unresolved.
7. The customer's account was weighed against all systems, with contradictions named - verified; the only contradiction is the customer's count of 15 versus the 12 local Error rows, settled by the provider showing exactly 15 failed accounts.

## Unverified

* The customer's preferred remedy (money back versus account credit) has not been stated in the conversation. It decides the form of the proposal, not its merit.
* Whether he wants the 15 inboxes replaced after all, given that replacement is a new paid provisioning action while his account already bills for 36 inboxes.
* The exact start date of lost sending for each of the 15; local webhook history is empty and provider timestamps are the closest available signal.

## Observations

The product defect behind this ask is confirmed and already tracked as an open engineering master; a customer report for this conversation is raised separately and parented to that master. Do not bury the defect inside this billing record.

relatedSnapshot.title: Switching the theme doesn't work on any subpages of /workflows
relatedSnapshot.description:
Open workflows page or any of the tabs or any workflow and press "T" on the keyboard to switch the theme. Nothing happens

Try anywhere else, the theme will switch

I remember I merged a PR that was explicitly disabling switching theme when an input field was highlighted but I made sure it worked outside (and it did) so it might've regressed somehow

---

## Implementation Plan (Name 22)

### Summary of Current Code

**Background Context:** The app has a global `CommandPaletteProvider` (mounted at dashboard layout level) that registers keyboard shortcuts via a custom `useHotkeys` hook. The 'T' key toggles the theme between light/dark using `next-themes`. The hook delegates to `isEditableElement()` in `keyboard-utils.ts` to skip hotkeys when the user is typing in form controls or interacting with Radix UI overlays.

**Current Behavior:**

* On workflow editor pages (`/dashboard/{slug}/workflows/{id}`): The 'T' hotkey is completely disabled via `isWorkflowEditorPage` in the `enabled` option. This was added in ENG-6118 (commit `e59c458c2`) to prevent shortcuts from hijacking dropdown/menu interactions. However, the workflow editor only handles Ctrl/Cmd combos + Backspace/Delete/Enter — no 'T' key conflict exists.
* On the workflow list page (`/dashboard/{slug}/workflows`): The hotkey IS enabled, but group expand/collapse buttons have `aria-expanded="true"`. The `isEditableElement` function treats any element with `aria-expanded="true"` as editable, blocking the hotkey when these buttons have focus.

**Key Components:**

* `CommandPaletteProvider` — registers all keyboard shortcuts including theme toggle
* `useHotkeys` hook — manages keydown listeners with `enabled` gate + `isEditableElement` guard
* `isEditableElement()` — determines if focused element should suppress hotkeys
* `isWorkflowEditorPage` regex — URL-based check that blanket-disables shortcuts on editor pages

### Affected Files

| File | Change Needed |
| -- | -- |
| `components/command-palette/command-palette-provider.tsx` | Remove `isWorkflowEditorPage` from the theme toggle's `enabled` condition (line 161). Consider whether navigation shortcuts (g→s, g→u, g→o) should also be re-enabled on editor pages since they don't conflict either. |
| `lib/keyboard-utils.ts` | Narrow the `aria-expanded="true"` check (lines 70-73) so it only blocks hotkeys for actual Radix UI trigger elements with open popups, not generic expand/collapse buttons. Also remove dead code on line 72 (`return false` after `return true`). |
| `tests/lib/command-registry.test.ts` | Existing tests — no changes needed but consider adding `isEditableElement` unit tests |

### System Overview

```
User presses 'T'
  → window keydown event
  → useHotkeys handler (command-palette-provider.tsx)
    → Gate 1: enabled check — !(open || isOnboarding || isWorkflowEditorPage)
    → Gate 2: isEditableElement(event.target) via use-hotkeys.tsx
    → Gate 3: callback checks activeElement for INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable
  → setTheme(newTheme) via next-themes
  → toast notification
```

**Connections:** `CommandPaletteProvider` wraps the entire dashboard layout. `useHotkeys` attaches a global `window.addEventListener('keydown')`. `isEditableElement` is shared across the hotkey system. The workflow editor has its own independent keydown handler on `window` that does NOT interfere with the theme toggle.

**External deps:** `next-themes` v0.4.6 (theme state), Radix UI (component library, source of `aria-expanded` attributes)

### Edge Cases and Name 21

1. **Radix UI overlays must still be protected:** The `aria-expanded` check exists to prevent hotkeys from firing when a Select dropdown or DropdownMenu is open. Any fix must preserve this behavior. The key distinction: Radix triggers with open popups vs. generic expand/collapse buttons.
2. **Multiple hotkey registrations use** `isWorkflowEditorPage`: Lines 161, 176, 187, 202 all reference it. The ticket is specifically about theme toggle, but the same blanket disable affects navigation shortcuts (g→s, g→u, g→o). Consider fixing all four or just the theme toggle.
3. **Dead code in keyboard-utils.ts:** Line 72 has unreachable `return false` after `return true` on line 71. This should be cleaned up.
4. **No auto-focus on workflow pages:** Verified that no elements auto-focus on either workflow page, so the issue only manifests after user interaction (clicking expand/collapse buttons).
5. **Command palette Name 23+K path unaffected:** Theme toggle via the command palette search (Name 23+K → "Toggle Theme") works independently and is not affected by this bug.

### Key Considerations

* **Pattern:** The codebase already has the `isEditableElement` function as the canonical way to detect when hotkeys should be suppressed. The `isWorkflowEditorPage` blanket disable was a shortcut that bypassed this pattern.
* **Constraint:** The `useHotkeys` hook already has `allowInInput` option and `isEditableElement` guard — the fix should leverage these existing mechanisms rather than adding more URL-based checks.
* **Backwards compat:** The Radix overlay detection (role checks, `data-radix-popper-content-wrapper`, etc.) must continue working correctly.
* **Performance:** No performance concerns — all checks are synchronous DOM queries on keydown events.

### Suggested Approach

1. **Fix** `keyboard-utils.ts` first: Narrow the `aria-expanded="true"` check to only match elements that are actual Radix UI triggers with open overlays (e.g., check if element has `data-radix-*` attributes or if a `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` exists in the DOM). Remove the dead code on line 72.
2. **Fix** `command-palette-provider.tsx`: Remove `isWorkflowEditorPage` from the theme toggle's `enabled` condition. Evaluate whether to also remove it from navigation shortcuts (g→s, g→u, g→o) since they also don't conflict with editor shortcuts.
3. **Testing strategy:**
   * Unit test `isEditableElement` with various element types (expand button with aria-expanded, Radix Select trigger with aria-expanded, input, textarea, contentEditable)
   * Manual E2E: verify theme toggle works on both workflow pages, verify it's still blocked inside Radix Select/DropdownMenu overlays, verify it's blocked while typing in inputs

### Open Questions

1. Should we remove `isWorkflowEditorPage` from ALL hotkey registrations (theme + navigation shortcuts) or just the theme toggle? The ticket specifically mentions theme, but the same issue affects g→s, g→u, g→o.
2. What's the best heuristic to distinguish Radix trigger elements (should block) from generic expand/collapse buttons (should not block)? Options: check for `data-radix-*` attributes, check if a popper wrapper exists in DOM, or check for specific roles.
